title: Paths for Democratic Control
dek: Democrats' majority path starts with holding Michigan and flipping North Carolina and Maine, then runs through Ohio, Texas, or Alaska.
author: Senate Probability Desk
body: In 2026, Democrats start at a disadvantage: more than twenty of the thirty-five seats up for election are in states Trump carried by more than five points. Still, Trump's weak approval and Democratic overperformance in 2025 and early 2026 elections give the party a narrow Senate path.

In almost any Democratic majority scenario, North Carolina and Maine have to flip. The current forecast gives Maine about a 71% chance of electing a Democrat and North Carolina an over 88% chance of electing former Gov. Roy Cooper, making those two races the foundation of the Democratic path.

If Democrats flip North Carolina and Maine, Michigan becomes vital to hold. The state has a close three-way Democratic Primary, and the eventual nominee is likely to face Mike Rogers in a tough election. Even so, the model currently gives Democrats roughly a 70% chance of holding the seat.

That would leave Democrats needing two more flips, most likely from Ohio, Texas, and Alaska. Ohio is the clearest opportunity, but the forecast still treats it as close. Texas and Alaska are harder, but either could flip if the national environment keeps moving toward Democrats.
